chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Fuzayl ibn Ghazwan, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so Al-Tayyar said to him, 'I found a dinar during the circumambulation whose writing had been obscured.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is for him.'

key_terms.الطَّوَافِ: Circumambulation, the ritual walking around the Kaaba
key_terms.الطَّيَّارُ: Al-Tayyar, a specific companion or narrator known by this title
key_terms.انْسَحَقَ: To be rubbed out, erased, or obscured
key_terms.دِينَاراً: A gold coin, used here as a generic term for currency or valuable item
key_terms.كِتَابَتُهُ: Its writing, inscription, or mark of ownership

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a lost item found in the Haram if the owner's mark is unclear?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *ghasb* (possession) for lost property found within the Haram when the owner's mark (*kitabah*) is obliterated. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the sanctity of the Haram does not automatically transfer ownership to the finder, but rather relies on the presumption of the owner's despair (*istishab al-ghaib*) when identification becomes impossible. It serves as a foundational precedent for the legal category of *al-luqata* (foundations) in Shia fiqh, distinguishing between items with clear ownership markers and those without.
